facts.raw_span: A woman in her 40s presented with a 10-year history of progressive skin thickening and subcutaneous enlargement of the right side of her nose and right cheek
she had undergone nondiagnostic skin biopsies
she underwent a septorhinoplasty 6 months prior due to collapse of her right nasal ala
significant submucosal tissue was noted and removed from the right nasal cavity
she initially improved but noticed enlargement of soft tissue with thickening of the overlying skin on her right cheek and right side of her nose several months later
slightly hyperplastic soft tissue with dilated patulous follicles involving the right medial malar cheek and right nasal ala in addition to deviation of the nasal tip
initial septorhinoplasty specimens showed fibroadipose tissue and vascular proliferation
initial skin biopsy was interpreted as sebaceous hyperplasia
subcutaneous-based proliferation of spindle cells with varying density
thickened and fragmented collagen bundles
mature adipocytes extending into skeletal tissue
spindle cells had bland cytomorphology with tapered nuclei and ill-defined cytoplasm
no cellular pleomorphism observed

she had undergone nondiagnostic skin biopsies

concepts.why: The presence of subcutaneous-based proliferation of spindle cells with varying density, thickened and fragmented collagen bundles, and mature adipocytes extending into skeletal tissue supports this diagnosis
The initial skin biopsy was interpreted as sebaceous hyperplasia, which is a type of dermal hypoplasia
The presence of fibroadipose tissue and vascular proliferation, as well as mature adipocytes extending into skeletal tissue, supports this diagnosis
The presence of thickened and fragmented collagen bundles supports this diagnosis
The presence of subcutaneous-based proliferation of spindle cells with varying density and mature adipocytes extending into skeletal tissue supports this diagnosis
The presence of subcutaneous-based proliferation of spindle cells with varying density and mature adipocytes extending into skeletal tissue supports this diagnosis
The presence of spindle cells with bland cytomorphology and tapered nuclei is consistent with Spindle Cell Lipoma.

rationales.F01: Progressive skin thickening and subcutaneous enlargement suggests a possible hamartomatous or lipomatous process.
rationales.F06: Hyperplastic soft tissue with dilated patulous follicles is not typical of sebaceous hyperplasia.
rationales.F07: Fibroadipose tissue and vascular proliferation are characteristic of nodular fasciitis and fibrolipomatous hamartoma.
rationales.F08: Sebaceous hyperplasia is less likely given the clinical and histological features.
rationales.F09: Subcutaneous-based proliferation of spindle cells is characteristic of nodular fasciitis and fibrolipomatous hamartoma.
rationales.F10: Thickened and fragmented collagen bundles are seen in various fibrous and lipomatous lesions.
rationales.F11: Mature adipocytes extending into skeletal tissue is a distinctive feature of fibrolipomatous hamartoma.
rationales.F12: Bland cytomorphology with tapered nuclei and ill-defined cytoplasm is characteristic of spindle cell lipoma and fibrolipomatous hamartoma.

frontier_selector.rationale: The combination of progressive skin thickening, subcutaneous enlargement, and the presence of mature adipocytes extending into skeletal tissue, along with the histological findings of spindle cells and thickened collagen bundles, best supports Fibrolipomatous Hamartoma as the diagnosis.
